chain.label: 737 main rudder PCU dual-concentric servo valve with tight clearances, not reliably redundant
chain.trigger: The dual-concentric servo valve used in all Boeing 737 main rudder power control units is not reliably redundant.

chain.label: Servo valve slides can overtravel beyond design range, misporting hydraulic fluid
chain.trigger: Both the primary and secondary slides are designed so that they can move about 0.018 inch axially beyond their normal operating range (overtravel capability).

caused_by.evidence: the servo valve secondary slide could jam to the servo valve housing at a position offset from its neutral position without leaving any obvious physical evidence

chain.label: Certification and acceptance testing failed to detect the reversal failure mode
chain.trigger: The Safety Board is also concerned that the potential for this aberrant operation of the B-737 rudder MPCU was not found during the unit's initial design acceptance tests or during the postproduction functional tests of individual units.

caused_by.evidence: the Boeing 737 rudder system design certificated by the Federal Aviation Administration is not reliably redundant

chain.label: Strong westerly flow over the Front Range west of the approach path
chain.trigger: Strong winds aloft created complex airflow patterns that moved from west to east across the mountains located west of the airplane's flightpath

chain.label: Moderate turbulence and gusty winds on final approach to runway 35
chain.trigger: During the approach to COS and prior to the right roll, flight 585 encountered moderate turbulence below 9,000 feet.

caused_by.evidence: these airflow patterns likely included strong turbulence, eddies, rotational flow fields, and crosswind shear

chain.label: Crosswind gust produced sustained uncommanded right yaw at ~4.7 deg/sec
chain.trigger: the airplane's right yaw rate had reached 4.7 deg per second just before the rudder reversal because of the effects of a wind gust

caused_by.evidence: In its computer simulation, the Safety Board matched this heading change by introducing a crosswind gust component, resulting in right yaw.

chain.label: Secondary slide jammed to servo valve housing offset from neutral
chain.trigger: a jam of the main rudder power control unit servo valve secondary slide to the servo valve housing offset from its neutral position

caused_by.evidence: as a result of some combination of tight clearances within the servo valve, thermal effects, particulate matter in the hydraulic fluid, or other unknown factors
the potential for this aberrant operation of the B-737 rudder MPCU was not found during the unit's initial design acceptance tests

chain.label: Captain applied left rudder pedal to arrest the uncommanded right yaw
chain.trigger: the captain responded to the sudden, rapid, and sustained heading change by applying left rudder pedal input about 0943:32

caused_by.evidence: This sustained yaw would have been apparent to the captain as motion of the ground and sky features relative to the fixed reference of the airplane's windshield area.

chain.label: Rudder reversed and deflected right to its blowdown limit, opposite the pilot command
chain.trigger: The rudder surface most likely deflected in a direction opposite to that commanded by the pilots as a result of a jam of the main rudder power control unit servo valve secondary slide

caused_by.evidence: when the secondary slide was jammed to the servo valve housing and a sufficiently high-rate force was applied on the input crank, compliance within the rudder system could allow the primary slide to overtravel and result in a reverse rudder command
This scenario further assumed that this input occurred while the main rudder PCU servo valve secondary slide was jammed to the servo valve housing, resulting in a rudder reversal to the right.

chain.label: Captain initiated a go-around, dividing his effort between thrust levers and controls
chain.trigger: the captain signaled his decision to abandon the approach by stating 'fifteen flaps'

caused_by.evidence: a flight control difficulty, such as that produced by a rudder reversal, would have been consistent with the captain's speed and urgency in making this decision

chain.label: No procedure or training existed for recognizing and countering a rudder reversal
chain.trigger: such training was not yet developed and available to the flight crews of USAir flight 427 or United flight 585

caused_by.evidence: Pilots would be more likely to recover successfully from an uncommanded rudder reversal if they were provided the necessary knowledge, procedures, and training to counter such an event.

chain.label: Delayed full left control wheel input while contending with the reversing pedals
chain.trigger: it would be understandable for the captain to have initially made a partial wheel input while contending with the powerful physical and mental demands of the problem with the rudder

caused_by.evidence: the captain of United flight 585 would have been contending with the distraction of the malfunctioning rudder and thus would have been devoting his physical effort to overpowering the rudder pedals
the captain would have been using his right hand to advance the thrust levers for an attempted go-around... only his left hand available to rotate the wheel to the left
These circumstances would have been extremely confusing and distracting and would have been unknown to the flight crew based on previous experience.

chain.label: Upset began below 1,000 feet agl on final approach, leaving no recovery margin
chain.trigger: because the United flight 585 upset occurred when the airplane was less than 1,000 feet above the ground, the pilots had very little time to react to or recover from the event

chain.label: Uncontrolled right roll to inverted with nose-down pitch
chain.trigger: the airplane rolled steadily to the right and pitched nose down until it reached a nearly vertical attitude

caused_by.evidence: a loss of control of the airplane resulting from the movement of the rudder surface to its blowdown limit
by about 0943:35, only 3 seconds after the reversal, the right bank angle had increased to more than 80 degrees
the pilots had very little time to react to or recover from the event

chain.label: Near-vertical impact with terrain 3.47 nmi south of runway 35 and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: impacted terrain 4 miles south of Colorado Springs Municipal Airport

caused_by.evidence: Ground impact occurred about 5 seconds later, only 9 seconds after the rudder reversal began.

chain.label: All 25 occupants fatally injured
chain.trigger: The 2 flight crewmembers, 3 flight attendants, and 20 passengers aboard were killed

caused_by.evidence: The cause of death for the 20 passengers and 5 crewmembers was determined to be blunt force trauma.
